newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND BANK SEES 97-98 CPI RISE BELOW 2 PCT - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND BANK SEES 97-98 CPI RISE BELOW 2 PCT - PAPER.

text.p: Bank of Finland governor Sirkka Hamalainen was quoted as saying in an interview with Central Banking magazine received on Friday that Finnish inflation would remain below or near two percent in the next one or two years.
"In 1996 the inflation rate will be about one percent and we expect it to remain under two percent or thereabouts in the next one or two years," she said.
"Expectations of future inflation are very low," she said.
"There is general acceptance throughout the government and the unions that it is vital to keep inflation low," she added.
The Bank of Finland was maintaining its inflation target -- a core inflation rate around two percent, Hamalainen said.

"In spite of the ERM we are keeping an inflation target as a basic monetary policy objective," she said, referring to the linking of the Finnish markka to Europe's exchange rate mechanism last October," she said.
Hamalainen said the Bank of Finland was not expecting any conflict to arise between its exchange rate stability and low inflation targets.
But if such a conflict emerged, "of course the exchange rate takes priority," she said.

"Actually the difference between using monetary aggregates or exchange rates or inflation targets are very small. Basically these targets are very similar. With monetary and exchange targeting you also have an implicit inflation target," she said.
